value.name: bring hidden pages into corridor
value.description: Lucia brings a stapled packet of facility pages into the corridor and holds them out to Asha.
evidence: Lucia shifted her bag from her shoulder, unzipped it without looking up, and drew out a thin sheaf of stapled pages that she held out to Asha at chest height, the printed header of the facility visible along the top margin.

value.name: Asha receives facility documents
value.description: Asha takes the pages from Lucia and is struck by the fact that Lucia carried them in her bag.
evidence: Asha took them, and the weight surprised her less than the fact that Lucia had carried them in at all, folded into the same bag that had held the letter the night before.

value.name: Asha admits she has not opened email
value.description: After glancing at the top page, Asha says she has not opened the email yet and asks Lucia what changed.
evidence: She looked at the top sheet for only a moment before she said, quietly, that she had not opened the email yet, that the week had gone the way it had gone, and asked Lucia to tell her what had changed.

value.name: Lucia hesitates after handing over pages
value.description: Lucia briefly keeps her hand near the bag as if unsure she handed the pages over in the right order, then lets it drop.
evidence: Lucia's hand stayed near the bag a beat longer, as if she had not decided whether handing them over had been the right order of things, and then she let it fall to her side.

value.name: Asha comforts Lucia physically
value.description: Asha touches Lucia's forearm and asks her to explain what the pages mean.
evidence: Asha set her fingertips lightly on Lucia's forearm, just above the cuff of her sleeve, and asked her to say what the pages actually meant.

value.name: Lucia explains staffing cuts
value.description: Lucia says staffing levels dropped last month and the facility is no longer really providing specialized care.
evidence: Lucia did not pull away, but she did not look up either; she took a shallow breath, fixed her gaze somewhere near Asha's shoes, and said that the staffing levels had dropped last month and that they weren't really providing the specialized care anymore.
